text: Writing clean code is an important skill for every programmer. Clean code is easy to read and understand, which saves time for everyone who works with it. One key habit is following naming conventions: use clear, meaningful names for variables and functions so others can guess what they do. Another important idea is keeping functions small and focused on one task. This makes them easier to test and reuse. Finally, clean code is maintainable, meaning it is simple to update or fix later. When you write readable code from the start, you and your team avoid confusion and work more efficiently.
